 NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WZTV) — November is right around the corner, and folks across Middle Tennessee and Southern Kentucky know it's almost time to turn the clocks back an hour for the end of Daylight Saving Time.
 When everyone sets their clocks back the morning of November 1st, Nashville will go from a 7:09 a.m. sunrise and a 5:51 p.m. sunset on October 31st to a 6:09 a.m. sunrise and a 4:50 p.m. sunset on November 1st. The rest of 2026 will feature sunsets in the 4:00 hour and sunrises in the 6:00 hour, with the earliest sunset at 4:32 p.m. in early December and the latest sunrise coming just before 7 a.m. at the end of December.
 There has been a lot of talk over the years about making Daylight Saving Time permanent nationwide. If that change happens, the biggest effects would be seen in the winter months. The earliest sunset would shift later to 5:32 p.m. in early December and the latest sunrise would be close to 8 a.m. at the end of December and the beginning of January.
 The changes that would result from Daylight Saving Time being made permanent. (WZTV) 
 Lawmakers have taken up the issue several times. In 2022, the United States Senate passed the Sunshine Protection Act to keep Daylight Saving Time year-round, but the bill did not make it through the House and never became law. Earlier this year, the House passed a similar bill, but the Senate has still not acted on it.
 Tennessee has also shown its support for this change, putting a trigger law in place making it to where the state will observe Daylight Saving Time all year if the Sunshine Protection Act becomes federal law. The Uniform Time Act of 1966 currently blocks any state from adopting daylight saving time year-round without a change at the federal level.
 Action that has already been taken to make Daylight Saving Time year-round and what still needs to happen for the change to take place. (WZTV) 
So, after heading out for Halloween fun this Saturday night, don’t forget to roll those clocks back an hour before going to bed.
